extracted.intended_audience: experimental physicists and instrument-makers conducting and reading 19th‑century style optics and pendulum experiments (Royal Society readers)
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural criteria for designing, conducting, and reporting laboratory experiments in optics (reflected light, periodical colours) and in precision pendulum/vacuum measurements, including apparatus construction, calibration, control of variables, and data-reduction procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete apparatus description
rubrics_metrics.description: Give a detailed account of the apparatus: all pieces, dimensions, materials, and how they connect (e.g. pedestal, glass cylinders ground to fit, suspension plate, circular metal ring, bell glass, metallic pipe with stop-cock, stuffing-boxes, wires and cross-pieces, iron frame and stone piers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper describes the apparatus as 'six pieces' plus an iron frame and specifies dimensions (pedestal cylinder one foot high, plate 3 feet long by 16 inches broad, glass cylinders slightly conical, etc.). Reporting such particulars enables reproducibility and assessment of mechanical/thermal behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vacuum chamber sealing and joint protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure and describe how joints and seals are made and tested (e.g. rims ground to fit, joints secured with pomatum, withdraw air to press joints by atmospheric pressure, tighten screws before re-admitting air).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure: place glass cylinders in succession with joints made secure by pomatum; withdraw air so exterior atmosphere presses joints into closest contact; before re-admission, turn screws that connect the iron frame so that the suspension piece is firmly attached. Document sealing materials and order of operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leak detection and management
rubrics_metrics.description: Test pump efficacy and locate leaks; report observed leak behavior and any temporary measures when leaks remain (e.g. gauge rising an inch in several minutes, examine stuffing-box and metal cylinder).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform a preliminary trial of the pump, observe gauge rise rates, intercept communication to localize leaks, examine probable leak points (stuffing-box, metal), and describe how pumping was managed during runs when leaks could not immediately be fixed (pump gently, work intermittently to hold target pressure).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanical support and vibration isolation
rubrics_metrics.description: Secure the suspension and support structure to prevent extraneous motion (e.g. iron frame screwed to stone piers, strengthened by brackets) so the suspension point is effectively immoveable for precise vibration comparisons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report how the frame is anchored and braced; where immovable suspension is not possible, quantify expected small motions (elasticity of supporting bars) and justify why relative results remain valid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thermal management and avoiding mechanical stress
rubrics_metrics.description: Account for thermal expansion and avoid over-tightening parts that are constrained between rigid pieces (advice: loosen screws when temperature changes to avoid glass fracture; re-level planes after temperature change).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When glass pieces are tightly pressed between metal parts, do not leave screws excessively tightened across large temperature swings. Describe procedure for re-leveling and re-tightening after equilibration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instrumentation placement and description
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the placement and calibration of sensors and observation instruments (thermometers, mercurial gauge, barometer, telescope position, graduated arc and diaphragm placement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example placements: thermometer ball midway between axis and lower weight; telescope 18–20 feet from pendulums; graduated arc about 2 inches above iron cylinder; diaphragm tangents to disk as seen from telescope. Provide distances and mounting so readings are interpretable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calibration and conversion of measured scales
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide calibration details and conversion factors for recorded measures (e.g. registered arc must be multiplied by 0.845 to obtain the true arc; barometer corrections such as index +0.066 and reduction to standard temperature).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report how arc subdivisions map to actual displacement (degree length 0.73 inch, multiply read arc by .845), apply index and temperature corrections to barometer, and state conversion factors used in data reduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arc measurement protocol for pendulum
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify exact method to register arc of vibration: note points on graduated arc opposite tailpiece at each extremity, compute semi-arcs on both sides, average to obtain registered arc, then apply conversion to true arc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed protocol included: measure both sides of tail-piece, take mean of two semi-arcs as registered arc, then multiply by .845 to obtain the true arc; report all intermediate readings so conversion is transparent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observation timing and coincidence method
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a coincidence observation method (telescope) and report times of disappearance and re-appearance of coincidences, intervals between coincidences, and how those map to vibrations per diem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record times of disapp. and re-app. of coincidence events, compute intervals and mean values, and document telescope/detector geometry enabling coincidence observations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pressure control and record-keeping during runs
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain, monitor, and record the pressure gauge (e.g. keep near 7 inches), document how pump operation compensated leaks, and record thermometer changes during pumping.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe pump working schedule (e.g. worked in alternate intervals early on, then more continuously), note gauge fluctuations, and maintain contemporaneous records of gauge, thermometer, and times of observations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thermometer correction for pressure changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply and document corrections to thermometer readings caused by removal of atmospheric pressure (given corrections: near vacuum +0.75; for 7 inches +0.70; for 15 inches +0.5; for 20 inches +0.4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justify corrections experimentally (immersing thermometer in ice under receiver and observing fall upon exhaustion) and apply specified additive corrections when reducing temperatures measured inside the receiver to compensate for pressure effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of control (doubly enclosed) thermometers
rubrics_metrics.description: Include hermetically sealed control thermometers inside a secondary enclosure to verify that observed thermometer changes are due to external pressure rather than other causes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspend sealed control thermometers alongside the standard thermometer inside the vacuum apparatus; if sealed controls remain steady while standard thermometer falls on evacuation, use that to justify applied pressure corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative experimental design (air vs. rarefied)
rubrics_metrics.description: Make comparative measurements with the apparatus under full atmospheric pressure and under rarefied conditions (vacuum), including before-and-after air runs with the same setup to isolate the effect of air density.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Run pendulum in air, then in rarefied medium, re-admit air and re-run; use mean of before-and-after air runs to represent baseline and compute difference attributable to reduced pressure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Barometer calibration and capillarity correction
rubrics_metrics.description: Calibrate barometer against standards and apply index/capillary corrections (example: an index correction +0.066 was applied to Mr. Browne’s barometer when compared to Royal Society/Observatory standards).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe intercomparisons with standard instruments, state corrections applied, and include any reductions to standard temperature (e.g. reduction to 32°) used in analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compute and report buoyancy/air-density corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute corrections to pendulum vibrations due to buoyancy of the atmosphere (use specific gravity of pendulum, weight ratios, expansion of air) and report the reduction to vacuum expressed in vibrations per diem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: with specific gravity ~8.6 and weight ratios of water to air, derive a correction for buoyancy corresponding to a 30-inch atmosphere; show algebra/values used so readers can reproduce corrected vibrations per diem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantify and report experimental uncertainties and imperfections
rubrics_metrics.description: Document limitations of apparatus (e.g. imperfect pump, leaks, small motion of support due to elastic bars), their measured magnitudes (e.g. gauge rising rate), and justify how they affect (or do not prejudice) comparative results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When absolute immobility is not achieved, provide evidence (comparisons of results) that relative measurements remain reliable. State numerical uncertainties and corrections applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surface preparation, history, and its effects (optics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report surface treatment of optical components (grinding, polishing, heating, exposure to air), and note observed changes in optical behavior (periodic colours appearing/disappearing, tint changes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: a prism ground and polished at white heat ceased to give same periods; old fractured face gave fine colours while new fracture gave only one colour. Record surface age, treatment, and any attempts to alter or test it (boiling in acid, alkaline solutions, alcohol, pressure).

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple-method testing of surface-film hypotheses
rubrics_metrics.description: To test whether an invisible film causes observed optical effects, apply multiple probes (microscope, chemical cleaning, polarisation and total-reflection angle tests, pressing prisms into optical contact) and report negative or positive findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper reports fruitless attempts (no superficial tarnish visible microscopically; boiling in acids/alkali; alcohol; pressure) and presents cross-checks (polarisation and total reflection angles identical between prisms, optical contact causing change in observed colours) to assess the film hypothesis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-validation using independent optical tests
rubrics_metrics.description: Use independent optical measurements (polarising angle, angle of total reflection, optical contact experiments) to check whether surface films or refractive-power differences explain observed phenomena.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example procedures: measure polarisation angle, determine angle of total reflection with intervening oil, compare prisms cut from same plate; press prisms into optical contact to see whether orders of colours correspond to doubled film thickness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for crystalline anisotropy in interpreting colours
rubrics_metrics.description: When solids are crystallized minerals, relate observed tints to crystallographic axes/double refraction and treat the surface action as a mineralogical character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note that splendid colours in crystallized minerals are related to axis of double refraction; report mineral orientation and consider anisotropic refracting forces when interpreting periodical colours.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of controlled perturbations to test hypotheses
rubrics_metrics.description: Intentionally alter variables (e.g. temperature, grinding/polishing, pressure, optical contact, adding oils) and observe systematic changes to test causal relationships (temperature shifts minima, grinding changes observed periods, contacting films changes colours).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document how changing a single factor (slight temperature change shifts incidence of minimum from 85° toward 90°) affects the phenomenon; use such perturbations to support or refute hypothesized mechanisms (e.g. interference vs. surface film).
